title: Chromatic homotopy theory: telescopes, Morava K-theories and finite localizations
summary: Build the chromatic interfaces needed by purity in algebraic K-theory: finite p-local spectra, oriented coefficient theories, nilpotence and periodicity, telescopes, finite and chromatic localizations, Bousfield–Kuhn functors, generalized fiberwise homology, Morava E-theory, Tate blueshift, commutative-ring height, real K-theory, topological modular forms and James-filtered Thom spectra. Existing spectra, generic Tate theory and algebraic formal-module deformation theory are imported from their owners.
readme: This roadmap supplies chromatic homotopy theory for purity and other localizing-invariant consumers. Use K(0)=HQ and T(0)=S[1/p]; compare the two finite towers by a theorem on p-local inputs. Import spectra from H.5/H.6, monoidal categorical machinery from EDS, generic Tate from RT.2, complex K-theory from RT.4, algebraic formal modules and marked deformation rings from LubinTateFormalModulesAndQuasiCanonicalLifts, and the named layers of the current AlgebraicTopology and ModularCurves roadmaps. The target pass covers all fourteen layers; recorded proof gaps and supplier extensions prevent a closure claim. The reader document is definitive and the small suggested file states only formal-group point calculations whose carriers exist at the pins.

stages.title: Finite spectra and homological localization
stages.description:
Let Sp_(p) be spectra whose integer homotopy groups are Z_(p)-modules. Let FinSp_(p) be the idempotent-complete stable subcategory generated by S_(p) under finite sums, shifts and cofibers. Its objects are retracts of p-localizations of finite cell spectra; a finite spectrum here always means this compact stable notion.

For finite p-local V and p-local X, D V=F(V,S_(p)) is finite, V→D D V is an equivalence, and F(V,X)≃D V⊗X naturally in Sp_(p). Every spectrum in Sp_(p) is a filtered colimit of finite p-local spectra. The tensor-Hom formula with this p-local dual is not asserted for an arbitrary integral X.

For a spectrum E, an E-acyclic A satisfies E⊗A≃0; an E-equivalence has E-acyclic cofiber. An E-local Y has contractible Map(A,Y) for every E-acyclic A, equivalently Map(f,Y) is an equivalence for every E-equivalence f. Construct the accessible exact reflector L_E:Sp→Sp_E with unit η, natural initial among maps from X to E-local spectra. Define the Bousfield class ⟨E⟩ by its acyclics, with ⟨E⟩≤⟨F⟩ when every F-acyclic is E-acyclic. Smashing means L_E X≃L_E S⊗X compatibly with η.

stages.title: Oriented coefficient spectra and height
stages.description:
A complex orientation of a homotopy commutative ring spectrum E is x∈Ẽ²(CP∞) restricting to 1∈E⁰(*) under CP¹≃S². The projective-space comparison E*(CP∞)≃E*[[x]] is completed in the skeletal topology. Tensor product of line bundles defines a graded commutative one-dimensional formal group law F_E. For even-periodic E choose an invertible degree-two class to obtain a degree-zero coordinate and an actual Mathlib FormalGroup over π₀E.

For a commutative one-dimensional law over a characteristic-p field, its canonical continuous Z_p-action makes it an instance of the LT.0 formal-module notion: [p]_F has initial nonzero degree p^h, or is zero and has height ∞. Assign height zero where p is invertible. For an even-periodic p-local oriented ring E, geometric height at most n means this bound at every geometric point of Spec π₀E, with the orientation expressed in a degree-zero coordinate. For a general graded orientation, the sufficient uniform bound used here is the explicit condition (p,v₁,…,v_n)=π_*E on the invariant p-typical coefficient ideal. Coordinate change preserves these conditions.

Construct the Thom spectrum MU with universal complex orientation and π_*MU the Lazard ring with generator degrees doubled. At p, construct the p-typical retract BP of MU_(p), with π_*BP=Z_(p)[v₁,v₂,…] and |v_i|=2(p^i−1). Fix a p-typical coordinate and a standard generator convention; do not assert E∞ structures on BP or all its quotients.

For n≥1 construct BP⟨n⟩ and k(n) as BP-module quotients with π_*BP⟨n⟩=Z_(p)[v₁,…,v_n] and π_*k(n)=F_p[v_n]. Form E(n)=BP⟨n⟩[v_n⁻¹] and K(n)=k(n)[v_n⁻¹], with graded coefficients Z_(p)[v₁,…,v_(n−1),v_n^±1] and F_p[v_n^±1]. Set BP⟨0⟩=k(0)=HZ_(p), E(0)=K(0)=HQ, and K(∞)=HF_p. K(n) admits a unital homotopy-associative multiplication; no homotopy commutativity at p=2 or E∞ quotient structure is imposed.

For n≥1 there are BP-module cofiber sequences Σ^(2p^n−2)BP⟨n⟩→BP⟨n⟩→BP⟨n−1⟩ and Σ^(2p^n−2)k(n)→k(n)→HF_p, with first maps multiplication by v_n. Multiplication by p on BP⟨0⟩=HZ_(p) has cofiber HF_p. Inverting v_n in the first two middle terms gives E(n) and K(n). For every spectrum X, K(n)_*(X⊗Y)≅K(n)_*X⊗_(K(n)_*)K(n)_*Y; in particular K(m)⊗K(n)=0 for m≠n, including the stated endpoints 0 and ∞. For finite V, duality preserves vanishing of K(n)-homology.

stages.title: Nilpotence, type and periodicity
stages.description:
For n≥0 let C_n⊂FinSp_(p) consist of V with K(i)⊗V=0 for all 0≤i<n. A nonzero V has type n if V∈C_n and K(n)⊗V≠0; the zero object alone has type ∞. Each C_n is a thick tensor ideal. C_0 is all finite p-local spectra; C_1 is the finite rationally acyclic subcategory.

A map f:V→X with V finite is smash nilpotent if and only if K(i)_*f=0 for every i∈{0,1,2,…,∞}. A self-map of a finite spectrum is nilpotent under composition if and only if its action on every K(i)-homology is nilpotent. For an associative unital ring spectrum R and x∈π_*R, x is nilpotent if and only if its image in K(i)_*R is nilpotent for every i, including K(∞)=HF_p. State the integral version by varying the prime; here V and rings are p-local where the fixed-prime formulation is used. For the particular unit-detection consequence for p-local R, namely R=0 iff all K(i)⊗R=0, a unital magma in the homotopy category suffices; associativity is retained for the general graded-element formulation.

Every thick subcategory of FinSp_(p) is C_n for a unique n∈{0,1,…,∞}, with C_∞={0}. In particular a finite type-n object generates C_n under finite cofibers, shifts and retracts. There are finite objects of every finite type.

For n≥1 a v_n self-map of a finite p-local type-n spectrum V is a stable map v:Σ^d V→V with d>0, invertible on K(n)_*V and nilpotent on K(i)_*V for i≠n, including 0 and ∞. Record d, the map and its properties as data. At height zero use multiplication by p on the integral sphere as the separately specified degree-zero map; it is not a positive-degree self-map.

Every type-n finite p-local spectrum, n≥1, admits a v_n self-map. For a map f:V→W of finite spectra equipped with v_n maps, positive powers of the two self-maps can be chosen with equal suspension degree so that f commutes with those powers. Any two v_n self-maps on one finite spectrum have positive powers which agree after matching degrees. The relevant graded centrality may require further even powers; it is not strict centrality of the initial maps.

stages.title: Telescopes and periodic homotopy
stages.description:
Fix for n≥1 a type-n finite complex V_n and v_n:Σ^d V_n→V_n. Set T(n)=hocolim(V_n→Σ^(−d)V_n→Σ^(−2d)V_n→⋯), with arrows the desuspensions of v_n. Set T(0)=S[1/p]. The object depends on the pair; its Bousfield class does not. Do not replace T(0) by HQ except after restricting the argument to p-local spectra.

For n≥1 and a fixed unstable representative v:Σ^dV→V, define v_n⁻¹π_k(X;V) as colim_r π_(k+rd)Map_*(V,X) under precomposition with v, taking a tail where k+rd≥2 for spaces. For spectra use the stable mapping spectrum and integer grading. A v_n-periodic equivalence induces isomorphisms in every degree. At height zero, for spectra and simple spaces use π_*(X)[1/p]; it is a separate convention.

For n≥1: (a) X and Ω∞X have the same v_n-periodic groups; (b) any integer connective cover of a spectrum, and any finite connected cover of a space, is a v_n-periodic equivalence; (c) K(i)⊗T(n)=0 for i≠n, including i=0,∞; (d) T(n)-acyclicity implies K(n)-acyclicity; (e) S/p-acyclicity implies T(n)-acyclicity; (f) X→X_p^∧ is a T(n)-equivalence, for arbitrary spectra with the imported derived p-completion; (g) the Bousfield class of T(n) is independent of (V_n,v_n); (h) X is T(n)-acyclic exactly when all its v_n-periodic groups vanish. At n=0 retain only the separately justified p-inversion statements.

For n≥1 and any associative unital ring spectrum R, T(n)⊗R=0 if and only if K(n)⊗R=0. No such comparison is asserted for an arbitrary spectrum or for T(0) versus K(0).

stages.title: Finite localization and fracture
stages.description:
Write L_n=L_(K(0)∨⋯∨K(n)). On all spectra write L_n^f=L_(HQ∨T(1)∨⋯∨T(n)), so this includes p-localization, and write L_n^(p,f)=L_(S[1/p]∨T(1)∨⋯∨T(n)). For n=0 these are respectively HQ-localization and p-inversion. Construct units and tower maps L_n→L_(n−1), L_n^f→L_(n−1)^f and L_n^(p,f)→L_(n−1)^(p,f). The finite kernels and smashing property are theorems, not parts of the notation.

For n≥0, inside Sp_(p), ker(L_n^f)=Ind(C_(n+1)). Consequently finite localization in Sp_(p) is the localization away from a type-(n+1) finite spectrum, is smashing and preserves compact objects into the compact localized category. On all spectra ker(L_n^(p,f)) is the localizing subcategory generated by finite p-primary-torsion spectra of type at least n+1; it too is smashing. The kernel of L_n^f on all spectra additionally contains all q-primary finite spectra for q≠p.

If X is p-local then L_n^(p,f)X≃L_n^fX, naturally and compatibly with tower units and transition maps. Both outputs are p-local. Without p-locality the comparison is false, as S/q with q≠p shows. The functor called finite localization in Clausen–Mathew’s p-local convention is the L_n^f specified here.

Let E,F be spectra and assume L_E sends F-acyclics to F-acyclics. For every X the natural square L_(E∨F)X→L_FX over L_EX→L_E L_FX is cartesian. The hypothesis holds if L_E is smashing or if L_F kills every E-local spectrum. Apply it for 0≤m<n to E=T(0)∨⋯∨T(m) and F=T(m+1)∨⋯∨T(n), giving the finite-tower fracture square with upper-left L_n^(p,f)X and lower-left L_m^(p,f)X. The analogous p-local HQ convention follows by comparison.

If X is T(1)-acyclic, then L_1^(p,f)X→X[1/p] is an equivalence, without a p-locality assumption on X. In the p-local subcategory this says L_1^fX≃X⊗HQ.

stages.title: Bousfield–Kuhn functors
stages.description:
For a finite pointed complex V and a v_n map v:Σ^d V→V with n≥1, construct a spectrum-valued functor Φ_v on pointed spaces by repeating Map_*(V,−) along the v-induced degree-d structure maps. Its integer homotopy groups are v_n⁻¹π_*(−;V). Transport along compatible powers of self-maps and finite maps is coherently functorial, rather than a choice made only in the homotopy category.

For each n≥1 construct Φ_n:Spaces_*→Sp_(T(n)) with natural equivalences F(V,Φ_nY)≃Φ_vY for finite type-n V with self-map v, and Φ_nΩ∞X≃L_(T(n))X. The first comparison uses the finite mapping spectrum; the second is natural in every spectrum X. State uniqueness with the finite-source compatibilities, not merely the equality of homotopy groups.

For n≥1, if Σ∞Ω∞f is a T(n)-equivalence then f is a T(n)-equivalence. Indeed L_(T(n))f is a retract of Φ_nΩ∞Σ∞Ω∞f by the suspension-loop unit and counit. At n=0 the corresponding detection holds for maps of connective spectra with p inverted. The positive-height functor Σ∞Ω∞ does not in general preserve T(n)-equivalences: HZ is T(n)-acyclic whereas Σ∞Ω∞HZ=Σ∞Z has nonzero sphere summands.

stages.title: Connective spaces and generalized homology
stages.description:
Import the space Postnikov towers from H.3, including nontrivial fundamental-group action; only the comparison and indexing convention are owned here. For a pointed space X, construct τ_≤rX for r≥0 and the connected cover X⟨r⟩=fib(X→τ_≤(r−1)X) for r≥1. Then π_iτ_≤rX agrees with π_iX for i≤r and vanishes for i>r, and X⟨r⟩ has zero π_i for i<r. The tower converges for spaces. For a map, say m-connective when every homotopy fiber is (m−1)-connected, so π_i is an isomorphism for i<m and a surjection for i=m, at compatible components and basepoints.

For a fibration F→X→Y over a CW space and a spectrum E, filter E⊗Σ∞_+X by the inverse images of the skeleta of Y. The resulting homological spectral sequence has E²_(s,t)=H_s(Y; y↦E_t(F_y,+)) and d_r:(s,t)↦(s−r,t+r−1), with the full monodromy local system. Its total-degree target is π_(s+t)(E⊗Σ∞_+X). Assert strong convergence for a finite-dimensional base, or for a uniformly bounded-below fiberwise E-homology system; for arbitrary bases with periodic E state only the filtered object and conditional convergence criterion supplied by H.6.

Let f:X→Y be a map of spaces and E a spectrum. If for every y the augmentation E⊗Σ∞_+fib_y(f)→E is an equivalence, then E⊗Σ∞_+f is an equivalence, with no finiteness hypothesis on Y and no boundedness hypothesis on E. For pointed connected fibers the hypothesis says that their reduced E-homology vanishes. This theorem supplies the arbitrary-base comparison even when a periodic Serre spectral sequence has no established strong convergence.

For every n≥1 there is an integer m≥2 such that an m-connective pointed space whose v_i-periodic homotopy groups vanish for 0≤i≤n is L_n^(p,f)-acyclic after reduced suspension spectrum. Consequently an m-connective map of spaces which is a v_i-periodic equivalence for all 0≤i≤n induces an L_n^(p,f)-equivalence on suspension spectra. One can take m=n+1 using the Carmeli–Schlank–Yanovski height bound; keep this sharpened bound separate from Bousfield’s original dimension-dependent bound.

For n≥1, Σ∞Ω∞ preserves m-connective L_n^(p,f)-equivalences of spectra, where m is the bound of connective periodic vanishing, and in particular m=n+1 using the sharp bound. This does not assert preservation of arbitrary T(n)-equivalences.

stages.title: Morava E-theory and stabilizer actions
stages.description:
Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p and G a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height h≥1 over k. Import its marked universal deformation ring R(k,G), noncanonically W(k)[[u₁,…,u_(h−1)]]. Construct a K(h)-local even-periodic E∞ ring E(k,G) with π₀E=R(k,G), π_*E≅R(k,G)[u^±1], |u|=−2, and formal group the universal deformation of G. The realization space equipped with that deformation identification is contractible. The coefficient isomorphism and coordinate are choices, not canonical identifications.

Make E(k,G) functorial on the groupoid of perfect characteristic-p fields with specified isomorphisms of their height-h formal groups after coefficient transport. Aut(k,G) acts coherently through E∞ maps. For a Honda law over F_(p^h), specify the extended stabilizer G_h=Aut(G/F_(p^h))⋊Gal(F_(p^h)/F_p). Its action on coefficients is continuous for the maximal-ideal topology, and its finite subgroup restrictions are coherent finite actions usable in Tate and homotopy fixed points. A profinite action is not modeled as a discrete finite-quotient action on E_h.

stages.title: Chromatic localization and its limits
stages.description:
For n≥0, ⟨BP[v_n⁻¹]⟩=⟨E(n)⟩=⟨K(0)∨⋯∨K(n)⟩, with v₀=p. Moreover ⟨BP⟨n⟩⟩=⟨E(n)∨HF_p⟩ and ⟨k(n)⟩=⟨K(n)∨HF_p⟩ for n≥1. The formulas are statements of Bousfield classes, not equivalences of spectra.

Let R be a p-local even-periodic oriented homotopy commutative ring with geometric height at most n at every point of Spec π₀R. Then R and every R-module are L_n-local. The graded variant assumes the explicit unit-ideal criterion (p,v₁,…,v_n)=π_*R. The pointwise condition in the even-periodic case implies that criterion after converting the coefficients to degree zero. These statements require a uniform finite bound; no bound is inferred merely from having a one-dimensional law.

For every n≥0, L_nX≃L_nS⊗X naturally, compatibly with the localization unit. In the L_n-local category, E_n generates the unit as a thick tensor ideal: the E_n-based cobar totalization tower is pro-constant with value L_nS. Here E_n is Morava E-theory at height n≥1; treat height zero rationally. The pro-constant statement has uniform finite-stage retraction content, stronger than mere convergence of a spectral sequence.

For n≥1, every L_(n−1)-local spectrum is T(n)-acyclic. For every L_n-local X, the canonical comparison L_(T(n))X→L_(K(n))X is an equivalence. Both assertions require the stated chromatic locality and do not prove equality of the two localization functors on all spectra. The p-local chromatic level one agrees with KU_(p)-localization; globally L_KU detects all primes rather than a fixed-p tower.

At height one and every prime, the Bousfield classes of T(1) and K(1) agree. At every prime and every height n≥2, there exists a T(n)-local spectrum which is not K(n)-local. Thus a general-spectrum identification of the two theories is false. This node records the exact boundary on all comparisons; its higher-height proof uses algebraic K-theory and is a separately recorded gap, not a prerequisite of the ring acyclicity theorem.

For n≥0 and i>n, BP⟨n⟩ is K(i)-acyclic and T(i)-acyclic. For n≥1 the map BP⟨n⟩→E(n) is a T(n)-equivalence, and is also a T(i)-equivalence for i>n because both objects are acyclic there. It is not an L_n^f-equivalence in general: the rational homotopy of BP⟨n⟩ is connective, whereas E(n) has negative rational classes for n≥1.

stages.title: Norms, Tate spectra and blueshift
stages.description:
Import coherent finite-group orbits, fixed points, the normalized norm, its Tate cofiber, and the lax symmetric monoidal Tate functor from RefinedTraceMethods RT.2. For an E-local spectrum X with coherent G-action, the norm in Sp_E is L_E(X_hG)→X^hG, and its cofiber is L_E(X^tG). The fixed points are already E-local because local objects are closed under limits. The imported Tate module structure is compatible with this comparison. This node owns only the passage to the homological localization.

For a homological localization L and finite G, these are equivalent: every G-object in LSp has norm equivalence; L((LS)^tG)=0 for the trivial action on LS; the transfer Σ∞_+BG→S admits a section after L. If these properties hold for prime-order groups they hold for every finite group. The transfer Σ∞_+BC_p→S admits a section after Ω^(∞+1), by Kahn–Priddy in its cyclic-group form.

For n≥1, every finite group G and every T(n)-local spectrum X with coherent G-action, L_(T(n))(X^tG)=0. Equivalently L_(T(n))(X_hG)→X^hG is an equivalence. In particular the norm sequence becomes split after T(n)-localization. A raw Tate spectrum of a T(n)-local object need not vanish.

For n≥1, if X is L_n^(p,f)-local with a coherent C_p-action, then its raw Tate spectrum X^tC_p is L_(n−1)^(p,f)-local. The p-local HQ finite convention satisfies the corresponding statement. This lowers the upper finite-height bound by one and permits a further drop; it asserts neither zero Tate nor exact height n−1 for every X.

For the trivial C_p-action on p-complete complex K-theory, π₀((KU_p^∧)^tC_p)≅Q_p(ζ_p), including Q₂ at p=2. This is nonzero, whereas its T(1)-localization vanishes. For contrast request from RT.2 the Segal comparison mentioned in its tate-p-local-properties acceptance example: the trivial-action sphere Tate spectrum is the p-complete sphere, so a raw-sphere example cannot be substituted for a T(n)-local input in Kuhn’s theorem.

stages.title: Commutative rings and chromatic height
stages.description:
For height-(h+1) Morava E-theory E with π₀E=W(F_(p^(h+1)))[[u₁,…,u_h]] and a K(h+1)-local E∞ E-algebra R, construct the weight-p operation P:π₀R→R⁰(BC_p). It is multiplicative and unital, and becomes additive after quotienting by the transfer. The transfer generator in E⁰(BC_p)=E₀[[z]]/([p](z)) is [p](z)/z. For 1≤k<h, after reducing by I_(k+1)=(p,u₁,…,u_k), define g_(k+1) by [p](z)=z^(p^(k+1))g_(k+1)(z). If x maps to zero in π₀ of the iterated module quotient R/(p,u₁,…,u_k), then P(x) maps to zero in π₀ of R^BC_p/(p,u₁,…,u_k,g_(k+1)). These are module cofibers; no identification with ordinary ring quotients for arbitrary R is assumed. For R=E the regular coefficient case gives the quotient ring operation used in the valuation calculation. The k=0 Bockstein case is an explicit part of G14, rather than attributed to the printed k≥1 theorem.

For an E∞ ring spectrum R and h≥0, K(h)⊗R=0 implies K(h+1)⊗R=0. Consequently T(h)⊗R=0 implies T(h+1)⊗R=0 for h≥0, with T(0)=S[1/p]. For h≥1 translate by the ring-spectrum comparison; at h=0 use S[1/p]-acyclicity⇒HQ-acyclicity, not the false equality of these acyclic classes on all spectra.

For an E∞ ring R define ht_p(R)=inf{n∈Z | n≥−1 and T(n+1)⊗R=0}, valued in {−1,0,1,…,∞}; an empty set has infimum ∞. Hahn’s theorem makes the vanishing heights an upper interval. This definition uses T(0)=S[1/p] at the bottom, even for a ring not p-local; it differs from geometric height of an oriented formal group.

For an E∞ ring R with trivial C_p-action and i≥0, if L_(T(i))(R^tC_p)=0 then L_(T(j))R=0 for every j≥i+1. In particular T(i)-acyclicity of the trivial-action Tate spectrum forces T(i+1)-acyclicity of R. The action and coherent commutative structure are part of the hypotheses; no claim is made for an arbitrary group action on an arbitrary spectrum.

stages.title: Real topological K-theory
stages.description:
Construct periodic real K-theory KO from stable real vector bundles with the coherent direct-sum and tensor-product structures. Its zeroth infinite loop space is Z×BO. Use the real Bott class β∈π₈KO to make KO eight-periodic, and set ko=τ_≥0KO with its E∞ ring structure. The class β has its unique connective lift in π₈ko, and ko[β⁻¹]≃KO as E∞ rings. The complex theories ku and KU are the RT.4 input.

The nonnegative coefficient ring of ko is Z[η,α,β]/(2η,η³,ηα,α²−4β), with |η|=1, |α|=4, |β|=8. The coefficient ring of KO inverts β. For every prime and n≥1, ko→KO is a T(n)-equivalence, as is A→A[β⁻¹] for any ko-algebra A. This is a statement about the input spectra; the resulting algebraic K-theory purity belongs to the K-theory consumer.

stages.title: Topological modular forms
stages.description:
An elliptic cohomology theory is a triple (E,C,a) consisting of an even-periodic E∞ ring E, a smooth elliptic curve C over π₀E with trivialized cotangent line when a coordinate is chosen, and an isomorphism a between the associated oriented formal group and the completion of C at the identity. A coordinate is auxiliary; changing its trivialization transports the formal law by an LT.0 isomorphism. For a Weierstrass presentation the completed law is the existing WeierstrassCurve.formalGroup, hence its series is the reindexed formalAdd.

Let M̄_ell be the Deligne–Mumford stack of stable one-pointed genus-one curves with irreducible geometric fibers: smooth elliptic curves or nodal one-gons. On its étale site, construct the Goerss–Hopkins–Miller–Lurie sheaf Otop of E∞ rings. Its homotopy sheaves are π_(2r)Otop≅ω^⊗r and π_(2r+1)Otop=0. On an étale affine with a trivialization of ω the section ring is even-periodic and its formal group is the curve’s completed formal group; at the nodal boundary use the generalized elliptic formal group, of height one. The sheaf satisfies coherent étale descent; global sections may have odd and negative homotopy groups. Its algebraic generalized-elliptic boundary and the spectral sheaf/module carriers are explicit missing supplier inputs G16a–G16b; they are not supplied by the coarse compactification in the current ModularCurves roadmap.

Set Tmf=Γ(M̄_ell,Otop), tmf=τ_≥0Tmf and TMF=Γ(M_ell,Otop). These are E∞ rings with natural maps tmf→Tmf→TMF. The first map is the multiplicative connective-cover map; the second is restriction from the generalized-elliptic compactification to its smooth open. Global odd homotopy is permitted. Discriminant inversion is the separate comparison below.

For X=M̄_ell or M_ell equipped with Otop, global sections give a symmetric monoidal equivalence QCoh(X,Otop)≃Mod_(Γ(X,Otop)). In particular Γ on these quasicoherent spectral modules preserves all colimits. Tensoring a fixed spectrum V with a quasicoherent Otop-module is quasicoherent, and V⊗Γ(M)≃Γ(V⊗M). This theorem is specific to these spectral stacks; it is not ordinary affineness of the underlying algebraic moduli stack.

For each prime, Tmf_(p) and TMF_(p) are L₂-local. The maps tmf→Tmf are T(n)-equivalences for all n≥1, both spectra are T(n)-acyclic for n≥3, and Tmf→TMF is a T(2)-equivalence. Consequently tmf→TMF→L_(K(2))TMF are T(2)-equivalences. These statements concern the input spectra; their algebraic K-theory consequences stay with the purity consumer.

For a finite group G, a faithful G-Galois extension A→B of E∞ rings consists of a coherent G-action by A-algebra maps such that A→B^hG and B⊗_A B→∏_G B are equivalences, and tensoring with B is conservative on A-modules. Using the existing full-level-three elliptic moduli cover, construct TMF[1/3]→TMF(3) as a faithful GL₂(F₃)-Galois extension. Its p=2 localization has that same group, including determinant and residue-field components.

At p=2, L_(K(2))TMF(3)≃E(F₄,Ĉ) for a supersingular elliptic curve with a chosen full level-three marking, equivariantly for the induced GL₂(F₃) action, and L_(K(2))TMF≃E₂^hGL₂(F₃). At p=3, L_(K(2))TMF≃E₂^hG₂₄, where G₂₄ is the automorphism group of the supersingular pair over F₃, including the order-two residue-field Galois factor. Here |Aut(C/F₉)|=12 and the extended group has order 24. Choices of curve and marking give compatible equivalences, not an unmarked canonical coefficient-coordinate identification.

Choose the surviving discriminant class δ=Δ²⁴∈π₅₇₆Tmf, whose descent edge image is the algebraic modular form Δ²⁴. Then TMF≃Tmf[δ⁻¹], and at every fixed prime TMF_(p)≃Tmf_(p)[δ⁻¹]. This uniform exponent suffices; no assertion that Δ itself is an integral degree-24 class at primes two and three is used.

stages.title: James filtrations and Thom spectra
stages.description:
For a based well-pointed CW space W, J_rW is the space of words of length at most r in W, with occurrences of the basepoint removed; J₀W=* and J_∞W=colim_rJ_rW. Concatenation gives J_∞W a topological monoid. For connected W, J_∞W→ΩΣW is an equivalence, J_rW/J_(r−1)W≃W^∧r, and Σ∞J_∞W≃∨_(r≥1)Σ∞W^∧r. These are reduced suspension spectra. For W=S², J_rS² is the 2r-skeleton F_rΩS³.

For an E∞ ring R, GL₁R is the union of the unit components in Ω∞R with its multiplicative group-like E∞ structure, and BGL₁R→Mod_R classifies the R-lines equivalent to R. For f:X→BGL₁R, define Mf=colim_X L_f in Mod_R. A based n-fold loop map yields an E_n R-algebra structure on Mf by the monoidal Thom construction. Preserve the actual twist and coherent multiplicative data.

Let (S³)_p^∧ be the p-completion of the nilpotent space S³ and let f_p:Ω²(S³)_p^∧→BGL₁(S_p^∧) be the E₂ map extending the class 1−p∈π₁BGL₁(S_p^∧)=Z_p^× in the p-complete convention. Its p-complete Thom E₂ ring is HF_p. Set C_p=fib((S³)_p^∧→K(Z_p,3)), with the map inducing the identity on π₃. Restriction along Ω²C_p gives the p-complete Thom E₂ ring HZ_p. Here C_p is the 3-connected cover; using an uncompleted S³ with target K(Z_p,3) would give π₂=Z_p/Z instead. Thom tensor products and colimits in these assertions are taken in the p-complete symmetric monoidal category.

For m≥0 restrict f_p along ΩJ_(p^m−1)S²→Ω²S³→Ω²(S³)_p^∧ and denote the resulting p-complete E₁ Thom ring by y(m). All colimits in this family are colimits in p-complete spectra, formed by completing ordinary spectral colimits. Then y(0)=S_p^∧, there are E₁ maps y(m)→y(m+1), and colim_m y(m)≃HF_p. For m≥1, π₀y(m)=F_p. At p=2 and m≥1 define z(m) by restricting along Ω(J_(2^m−1)S²⟨2⟩), where the inner connected cover is the fiber of J_(2^m−1)S²→K(Z,2), followed by completion in the p-complete convention. These E₁ rings map to y(m), and colim z(m)≃HZ₂.

For m≥1, y(m) is L_(m−1)^(p,f)-acyclic: T(i)⊗y(m)=0 for 0≤i<m. At p=2, z(m) is K(i)-acyclic and hence T(i)-acyclic for 1≤i<m; its rational homology is nonzero, so do not add i=0 to that range.

Let W be a connected pointed CW space and let E=T(n)∨T(n−1), with n≥1. If E⊗Σ∞W=0 then E⊗Σ∞ΩΣW=0. In particular a connected type-m finite complex with m>n meets this hypothesis. This is the stable input for the corresponding Waldhausen A-theory purity application; no A-theory comparison is re-proved here.
